## Editor's Brief

The past 24 hours have been dominated by escalating Ukrainian deep-strike operations reaching as far as Saint Petersburg, a major legislative push for renewed U.S. aid to Kyiv, and intensifying military posturing in the Indo-Pacific and Middle East. Taiwan is accelerating its anti-ship missile arsenal, the Five Eyes alliance is sounding alarms over Chinese espionage tactics, and Washington is exploring unprecedented allied shipbuilding to relieve its strained naval industrial base. Meanwhile, the Middle East conflict marks its 100th day with Gulf states grappling with stability and new EU sanctions targeting Strait of Hormuz disruption.

- **U.S. House passes Ukraine Support Act** authorizing $8 billion in military loans and extending the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative through 2027, coupled with new sanctions on Russia ([Breaking Defense](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/06/house-passes-ukraine-aid-bill-with-new-sanctions-for-russia/)).
- **Ukrainian drones strike a Russian corvette near Saint Petersburg**, hitting the RFS Boiky while docked, marking a dramatic expansion of the conflict’s naval dimension ([Naval News](https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/06/ukrainian-drones-strike-russian-corvette-rfs-boiky-near-saint-petersburg/)). Ukraine also recorded its heaviest deep-strike month of the year, hitting 18 Russian oil and gas facilities ([Euromaidan Press](https://news.google.)).
- **Taiwan plans to boost its anti-ship missile arsenal to over 1,800 by 2029**, explicitly framing the buildup as a response to the Chinese invasion threat ([Taipei Times](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiekFVX3lxTE9tdjZlV2wxVkw2TEdLbVc5YzE3UjlEZC1iTGU2UGhIMGlMWTRnYUltWVFWbGJYS1pvMFA1WklmT3NnXzNqZUxvMVZGM2I5QzgyMS1VUDNxQ2lhNGxCZjVjTk84OUJPTVl0aTlIem8ySGZ6T1U1NmtTRjlB)).
- **Five Eyes intelligence alliance issues a joint warning** alleging Chinese operatives are using job recruitment platforms to recruit informants; Beijing dismisses it as “malicious slander” ([U.S. News](https://news.google.)).
- **The U.S. is considering procuring major naval vessels from Japanese and South Korean shipyards** to address capacity constraints, with a $1.85 billion funding request in the FY2027 budget ([Naval News](https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/06/u-s-eyes-warships-from-japanese-and-south-korean-shipyards/)).
- **The Iran conflict reaches 100 days** – Gulf states are grappling with stability and adapting alliances, while the EU expands sanctions to target Strait of Hormuz disruption ([DW](https://news.google.), [Pinsent Masons](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxPSGFfdzBnQXZyZFQ3bE5KVDFBY2Z2bGVvY3ZDdXBhNktGS0laczFwclVfQUFxT0NOY1cxMjJJOVczRjhJWERzSGFPTUhOcnUzQ0VhZTcyVnRiXzlNOXM4blRfeEFlOTh2ZWtraDdQUEUwUlhNZEVycU1Oc0lkYVBNcm5CUlk4WHJnbnc)).
- **The US Air Force accelerates plans for an MQ-9 Reaper replacement** that is modular and cheap, spurred by recent losses of the venerable drone ([The War Zone](https://www.twz.com/air/usaf-wants-mq-9-next-reaper-replacement-to-be-modular-cheap)).

**Watch next:** The next 48 hours will be critical for tracking the implementation of the Ukraine aid package and the ripple effects of the Saint Petersburg drone strike on Russian naval posture. In the Indo-Pacific, China’s reaction to Taiwan’s missile buildup and the Five Eyes allegations could escalate rhetorical or military responses. The U.S. House authorizers’ call for a battleship study and the allied shipbuilding initiative may signal a major shift in naval procurement strategy. Finally, watch for any new strikes in the Strait of Hormuz as the UK’s RFA Lyme Bay continues preparations.
